title: Context Windows, Prefill and the KV Cache
summary: A model reads its whole prompt in one parallel pass (prefill), then writes one token at a time (decode), reusing stored keys and values for every earlier token. That stored KV cache is what limits how many users and how much context fit on a GPU.
objectives: Explain what a context window is and budget a prompt, retrieved documents and output against it
Distinguish prefill from decode and explain why one is compute-bound and the other memory-bandwidth-bound
Compute KV-cache memory with 2·L·h_kv·d_h·n·B·bytes for a real model
Compare multi-head, grouped-query and multi-query attention by cache size and quality
Explain why facts in the middle of a long context are used less reliably, and what to do about it
prerequisites: You should know how attention computes queries, keys and values and applies a causal mask ([Attention](/learn/model-foundations/attention)), and what a transformer block contains ([The Transformer Block](/learn/model-foundations/transformer-block)). The decoding loop from [Next-Token Prediction and Sampling](/learn/model-foundations/sampling) is the loop we are about to make fast.
